content: The Oregon College of Oriental Medicine (OCOM), located in Portland, Oregon, United States, provides advanced educational programs, including master’s and postgraduate doctoral degrees, in the fields of acupuncture and Oriental medicine. The academic programs at OCOM are accredited by the Accreditation Commission for Acupuncture and Oriental Medicine (ACAOM). Additionally, the institution is authorized by the Oregon Student Assistance Commission’s Office of Degree Authorization to confer the degrees of Master of Acupuncture and Oriental Medicine (MAcOM) and Doctor of Acupuncture and Oriental Medicine (DAOM). OCOM operates an Intern Teaching Clinic and an herbal dispensary, which serve the Portland metropolitan area. This clinic provides over 20,000 low-cost treatments annually, including acupuncture, Chinese herbal medicine, tui na (a form of Chinese therapeutic massage), and shiatsu. The clinic also functions as a teaching facility, offering hands-on training for students enrolled in the college’s programs. In July 2005, OCOM achieved a significant milestone by becoming the first institution to graduate a cohort of students with Doctor of Acupuncture and Oriental Medicine degrees. The college maintains an active research department and has been the recipient of substantial research funding from the National Institutes of Health (NIH), specifically through the National Center for Complementary and Alternative Medicine (NCCAM). Current research initiatives at OCOM include a collaborative project with the University of Arizona, focusing on the study of temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders.
